name: Bavarian Illuminati
description: Real Enlightenment secret society founded by law professor Adam Weishaupt to promote reason against clerical influence, organized in Masonic-style grades. Banned by the Bavarian Elector by 1785 and effectively destroyed — yet posthumously credited with two centuries of world events it could not have witnessed.

name: Freemasonry
description: Fraternal order descended from stonemasons' guilds, with lodges, degrees, and private ritual. Its secrecy, elite membership (numerous founders, monarchs, and presidents), and iconography have made it the perennial subject of conspiracy literature — from the 1826 Morgan affair, which spawned America's Anti-Masonic Party, onward.

name: Skull and Bones
description: Yale senior society whose windowless 'Tomb' and roster of establishment figures (Tafts and Bushes among them) feed speculation about elite coordination. The documented reality is a networking society with theatrical ritual; the 2004 US election, contested between two Bonesmen, marked peak public fascination.

name: Bilderberg Meetings
description: Annual invitation-only conference of ~130 European and North American political, financial, and media figures, held under the Chatham House rule with no minutes published. Founded to shore up transatlantic relations; the secrecy that participants call candour is read by critics as covert world-steering.

name: Bohemian Grove
description: The Bohemian Club's redwood encampment where American business and political elites summer; its 'Cremation of Care' pageant before a forty-foot owl statue — infiltrated and filmed by Alex Jones in 2000 — supplied conspiracy culture's most vivid imagery of elite ritual. Documented reality: theatrical club tradition and significant informal networking (the 1942 Manhattan Project planning meeting did occur at the Grove).

name: Trilateral Commission
description: Policy forum founded by David Rockefeller linking North America, Europe, and Japan. A fixture of one-world-government literature since the 1970s; its published membership and reports make it among the least secret 'secret' organizations.

name: Central Intelligence Agency
description: US foreign-intelligence service whose documented covert history — coups in Iran (1953) and Guatemala (1954), MKUltra, assassination plots revealed by the Church Committee, media contacts — supplies the factual bedrock on which far larger undocumented claims are routinely built.

name: National Security Agency
description: US signals-intelligence agency so secret its existence was once denied ('No Such Agency'). The 2013 Snowden disclosures documented mass-collection programs (PRISM, bulk telephony metadata) that vindicated earlier 'paranoid' claims in part — reshaping the baseline of what surveillance theories are plausible.

name: FBI COINTELPRO
description: The FBI's real covert program to surveil, infiltrate, and disrupt domestic movements — civil-rights leaders, the New Left, Black Panthers — exposed when activists burgled the Media, Pennsylvania field office in 1971. A cornerstone example of an actual government conspiracy proven by documents.

name: Opus Dei
description: Catholic personal prelature emphasizing sanctification of ordinary work, with celibate 'numerary' members and historical practices of corporal mortification. Its discretion and influence in professional circles drew conspiracy portrayals — amplified enormously by The Da Vinci Code's fictional assassin-monk.

name: Majestic 12 (alleged)
description: The UFO-management committee said to have been chartered by Truman in 1947. Known only from documents the FBI judged bogus; listed here as an alleged organization because much later UFO lore treats it as real infrastructure.

name: Order of Assassins (Nizari Ismailis)
description: The medieval Nizari state run from mountain fortresses like Alamut, which practised targeted assassination of political enemies — the historical seed of countless secret-order legends (and the word 'assassin'), embellished by Crusader and Marco Polo-era tales of drugged gardens of paradise.
